Row.Text: Civilizations are remembered for their accomplishments and the paths they take through history. Some spread their accomplishments across a wide range, while others are devoted to a single cause. Your Advisors are at your service to guide you on the path of your choice. Like any great leader, you may change your mind at any time.
Follow
Unfollow
You can change your selection at any time by visiting the Advisor Council.

Council Room
Nothing to say.

Our settlement of {1_City} stands unguarded in these dangerous times — but not unnoticed. The forces of the {2_CivName} approach, and we must bare our fangs to protect the citizens. Send military units to this urban center immediately.
Defenseless Settlement

The enemy approaches our settlement of {1_City}, bearing the banners of the {2_CivName}. The garrison will defend our people to the end, but they are greatly outnumbered. Send reinforcements to swell their ranks.
Settlement Under Threat
The rulers of {2_IndependentName} are being swayed more and more by {1_LeaderName}. If we do not spend more Influence there, they will become a City-State under the suzerainty of our rivals!
Independent Being Lured Away
There is only so much administration one can assemble, and too many places for it to go. With our new Settlement, we have exceeded our Settlement Cap. Perhaps researching some new Civics might help.
Over Settlement Cap

Rumors abound that {1_CivAdjective} Technology is decades ahead of the rest of the world's. If we are to remain relevant in the scientific community, we must find a way to increase our own Science output.
Trailing in Technology

"What is the latest style in {1_CivName}?" It is a question I hear daily. They appear to be ahead of us by several Civics, and people are starting to take notice. Perhaps some more Culture output is in order?
Trailing in Civics

A well-run economy sails like a well-hulled ship. Ours is leaking Gold. To keep from sinking entirely, we must construct buildings that provide Gold, reduce our military, construct Towns in productive areas, or sign Open Markets deals with our neighbors.
Negative Gold Per Turn
Influence is squandered when hoarded. Its value lies in how it is traded. We should use our unspent Influence to strengthen Alliances and boost our trade yields!
Surplus Influence

One of our great Commanders is a hero to soldiers and civilians alike. Their battlefield ingenuity has earned them several promotions, but these have yet to be awarded. It is time they receive their rightful honors.
Promotions to Award

{2_City}, part of the {3_CivName}, is overflowing with valuable commodities and {1_Amount} resources. Thriving markets are a sign of thriving societies. To strengthen our own, we should dispatch a merchant to negotiate a trade agreement.
Trade Opportunity

{1_City} is brimming with discontent, and productivity is flagging. We should assign Happiness resources, station a Commander in the settlement, or invest in Happiness infrastructure here. With trust and confidence in your rule, Gold will flow once more.
Low Happiness
The bond between us and {1_LeaderName} is beginning to fray. If relations become Neutral, this Alliance will cease. We should strengthen our ties through a joint Diplomatic Endeavor.
Alliance Weakening

Our war efforts falter as {1_playerName}'s support in this conflict grows. At home, our people suffer a penalty to [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS]Happiness in our settlements. At the front, our soldiers endure a combat penalty when fighting {1_playerName}'s units. Let us spend [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY]Influence to increase support for our cause to reduce these negative effects.
Suffering War Weariness

The settlement of {2_CityName} is on the brink of Revolt. If they remain Unhappy for {1_Duration} turns, they may Revolt. We should assign Happiness resources, station a Commander in the settlement, or invest in Happiness infrastructure here immediately.
Settlement Revolt

Our rivals in {2_CivName} have plans drawn up and work begun on the World Wonder {3_ConstructibleName} — the very same as what we're building in {1_CityName}. They say hard work is its own reward, but let's try for a Wonder, too.
Competing Wonder

Your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Cultural Advisor[/TIP] provides recommendations, warnings, and tips for how to win a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP]. While you’re always in charge, your Advisor can be helpful if you’re ever at a loss for how to proceed. Even if you’re not pursuing the Cultural Victory, the Advisor can help you better understand cultural matters. [nn]You can access past messages as well as the messages of the other three Advisors from this screen. Check it often to learn important information about the game. [nn]Your Cultural Advisor is here to help you win the Cultural Victory, but if you’d like to follow a different Advisor or turn Advisors off altogether, you can do so from this screen.

Earning Tourism
Our empire falls behind in Tourism as the Age ends. If you need assistance, I am here.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP] will be coming to a close soon, and you’re currently behind in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP]. [nn]Remember, Tourism is gained from several sources, including constructing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] and your civilization’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP], having [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP] within your borders, and earning [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebrations[/TIP] after Researching Entertainment. [nn]Don’t worry – there’s still plenty of time to catch up! As this Age ends and the next begins, try to focus on activities that generate Tourism. [nn]And if all else fails, you can always slow the other leaders down. Consult your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Military Advisor[/TIP] if you’d like to pursue more direct intervention…

Earning Dominion Points
As the Age ends, we're caught on the back foot. But there's still plenty we can do to win the Military Victory.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP] will be coming to a close soon, and you’re currently behind in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP][b] Points[/b]. There are two ways to increase your score: peacefully or through war. [nn][b]Peacefully[/b] increasing your[b] Dominion Score[/b] can come from training Settlers and founding your own [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] or using [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] to incorporate [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP]. [nn][b]Aggressively[/b] increasing your [b]Dominion Score[/b] comes from conquering enemy [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Look for ones that are lightly defended and easy to pick off or particularly valuable, like a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP]. Then Declare War and take them for yourself. Don’t forget, you can try negotiating for more Settlements when you make peace at the end of a war. [nn]The Antiquity Age is the first of three, so it’s okay if you’re behind for now. There will be more opportunities to catch up later.

Earning Innovation
Our opponents eclipse our efforts in the Space Race, but there is still much we can discover before this Age ends.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP] will be coming to a close soon, and you’re currently behind in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPACE_RACE_TOOLTIP]Space Race[/TIP]. [nn]Remember, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP][b] Points[/b] are gained from several sources in the Antiquity Age, including displaying [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codices[/TIP], researching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP], and completing the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP] [b]Chart the Stars[/b] and [b]Spherical Earth[/b] in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP]. [nn]There’s still time to make progress before the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] comes to an end! Try to focus on activities that can earn Innovation. Once the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP] begins, there will be different activities that earn points and these ones will no longer be available.
Keep this in mind...

At this point in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], try to focus your research on [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP] that provide Victory Points or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codices[/TIP]. Check the [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] list in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] to see if you’re able to complete Chart the Stars or Spherical Earth [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP] before the Age ends. They’re both worth 5 points each.

Earning GDP
Time is money, and we are short on both. Let me show you how to earn more GDP.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP] will be coming to a close soon, and you’re currently behind in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP]. [nn]Remember, GDP is gained from several sources in the Antiquity Age after Researching the Currency Mastery, including having [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] like the [b]Market[/b] and [b]Lighthouse[/b] and for every [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] assigned. [nn]There’s still time to make progress before the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] comes to an end! Improve any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BONUS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Bonus Resources[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]City Resources[/TIP] the next time your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP], and make sure all available Resources are assigned. If you need more Resource Slots, construct Markets or Lighthouses.
Keep this in mind...

At this point in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], try to focus on quick sources of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP], like slotting available [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] or purchasing rather than producing Markets and Lighthouses. Remember, at the start of the next Age Markets and Lighthouses will no longer produce GDP.
Happiness
Happy Settlements contribute to Celebrations, which in turn attract Tourists.

[icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] is an important yield when managing your empire. Each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] independently earns [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] based on the Appeal of each improved tile, any [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] constructed, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] assigned, and other factors. The Settlement’s [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAINTENANCE_TOOLTIP]Maintenance[/TIP] is then deducted, resulting in the Settlement’s final [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] yield. [nn]If the yield is positive, the Settlement is considered Happy and any excess yield is used toward generating your next [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebration[/TIP]. [nn]If the yield is negative, the Settlement is considered Unhappy and suffers penalties. For each point of unhappiness, the Settlement receives a 5% penalty on all yields, with a maximum penalty of 80%. Certain Crises may increase these penalties even further, so don’t be too complacent with leading an unhappy empire. [nn]The most common cost of [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] is Maintenance from Buildings and [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP]. As you consider how to improve your Settlement’s infrastructure, pay attention to the [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] costs you’re introducing. Balancing [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] Maintenance with making your Settlements more productive is an important skill in the game. [nn]Your empire’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_LIMIT_TOOLTIP]Settlement Limit[/TIP] also plays an important role in [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b]. For each Settlement you are over the Settlement Limit, every Settlement receives a stacking -5 [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b]. This can add up quickly, so it’s important to manage your [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] well if you go over your limit!
Something to try...

If you have any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] suffering from negative [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b], look for easy sources to increase it. You may be able to purchase a [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] or move a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] to instantly fix it. The next [b]Growth Event[/b] may provide an opportunity to improve a tile with high Appeal. Consider setting a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP][b]’s Focus[/b] to Resort Town for a large [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] boost. [nn]Understanding the source of unhappiness is also important. Check to see if you’re over your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_LIMIT_TOOLTIP]Settlement Limit[/TIP], and if so look for ways to increase that. If you’re suffering from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_WEARINESS_TOOLTIP]War Weariness[/TIP], you may need to increase your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] or [b]Make Peace[/b].
Generating Culture
Beauty and Tourism thrive only if we can create enough Culture. Having Culture Buildings like Monuments and Museums will help.

[icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] is a yield that advances your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics Trees[/TIP], unlocking [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SOCIAL_POLICY_TOOLTIP]Social Policies[/TIP] that shape your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GOVERNMENT_TOOLTIP]Government[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] with powerful effects, and more. [nn]Construct [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] to increase how much [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] you generate each turn. Certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] and terrain features, including [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP], can also generate [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b]. In addition, certain leaders can start the Cultural Exchange Diplomatic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP], generating [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] for both parties. [nn]It’s important to generate a large amount of [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] if you want to win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP].
Something to try…

If you haven't yet, research the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] that unlocks [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] like Monuments, Kilns, and Museums. Place them near a Mountain, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonder[/TIP], or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonder[/TIP] to maximize their [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] yields!
Influence
Not everything has to be a competition. Use your Influence to begin Endeavors with other Leaders or befriend an Independent Power.

[icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] is one of the primary yields of the game. [b]Influence[/b] is earned through [b]Diplomacy [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], [b]Discoveries[/b] and [b]Narrative Events[/b], and being on the receiving side of a [b]Diplomatic Incident[/b]. [nn][icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] is a currency that is used for any kind of diplomatic action. A common use is to start, support, or reject [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SANCTION_TOOLTIP]Sanctions[/TIP], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ESPIONAGE_TOOLTIP]Espionage[/TIP]. These are powerful actions you take with or against the other leaders in the game. [nn]Another common use is to [b]Befriend [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Powers[/TIP]. This action is used on the Independent Powers on the map to convert them to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP], providing powerful bonuses to their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP] and unlocking further uses of [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b]. If you’re not looking to befriend an Independent Power, you can also use [b]Influence[/b] to [b]Incite Raid[/b] against another player, spawning a powerful army that they’ll have to deal with. [nn]While it may be wise to save up your [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] for the more expensive and powerful actions, like winning the race to Suzerain a City-State, banked [b]Influence[/b] doesn’t do anything for you. Knowing when to save up and when to spend your [b]Influence[/b] is an important skill in the game.
Something to try...

Early in the game when [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] is tight, think about what is most useful for your empire. A hostile [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Power[/TIP] on your borders may cause problems, so befriending them can allow you to focus on non-military actions. Starting and supporting friendly [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP], though, can greatly increase important yields, like [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b], [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b], and [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b]. Maintaining positive [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationships[/TIP] with your neighbors may help you avoid a costly war!
Settlement Limit
If we go over the Settlement Limit, we start taking Happiness penalties. Let's keep troop morale high.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_LIMIT_TOOLTIP]Settlement Limit[/TIP] represents the number of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] your empire’s administrators can manage before corruption or inefficiency kicks in. [nn]For each Settlement you go over the limit, every Settlement in your empire receives a -5 [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b][b] penalty[/b]. This limit is a soft cap, meaning that you can always choose to go over it, but the [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalty will increase endlessly, representing an ever greater challenge to overcome. [nn]Settlement Limit can be increased through a variety of means, including [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Techs[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP]. The Expansionist and Military [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attribute Trees[/TIP] also provide increases to Settlement Limit, as do [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedications[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP] Bonuses. If you’re looking to expand your empire and don’t want to suffer [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalties, look for ways to increase Settlement Limit.
Keep in mind...

Many civilizations are able to successfully manage their empire above the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_LIMIT_TOOLTIP]Settlement Limit[/TIP] by offsetting the [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalty with [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], and other ways of increasing [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b]. Successfully managing [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] is an important skill in the game, and a reward for doing so can be growing your empire beyond the Settlement Limit.
Alliances
If you Ally with another Leader, both will benefit. Strength through unity.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ALLIANCE_TOOLTIP]Alliances[/TIP] are formal agreements between two leaders showing the world they work together. [nn]To form an Alliance, you must first raise your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] level with another leader to [b]Helpful[/b]. Either party can then send a request to [b]Form Alliance[/b], and if the other side accepts, they are Allied. [nn]Allied leaders receive several benefits. They both automatically grant [b]Open Borders[/b] to each other. AI Leaders are also more likely to Support and Accept [b]Diplomatic [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP], and neither side can start a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SANCTION_TOOLTIP]Sanction[/TIP] against the other. Most importantly, Allied Leaders automatically get drawn into any War either party is a part of. [nn]When one side enters a War for any reason, the other party must decide to enter the [b]Joint War[/b] or end the Alliance. Joining a War in this way does not cause any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] penalties regardless of the Relationship the Ally had with the other Leader at the time of the War. Failing to meet the moment and ending the Alliance in the Ally’s time of need causes several Relationship penalties. [nn]An Alliance can also end if either party chooses to end it, and this becomes more likely when the Relationship erodes, so it’s important to maintain good Relationships if you want the Alliance to continue.
Something to try...

Raise your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] with another leader through positive interactions such as [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP] and Trade while minimizing the negative interactions until you reach Helpful. At that point, request to Form [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ALLIANCE_TOOLTIP]Alliance[/TIP] with the other Leader. If they view an Alliance with you as beneficial, they’ll accept.
War Support
Our efforts falter without vital War Support. Increase it with Influence in the Diplomacy screen.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] represents how much your people support your war and feel that it is justified. Having lower War Support than your enemy results in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] penalties and reduced [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] across your empire. As a result, it’s very important to maintain positive War Support during prolonged wars. [nn]When a leader [b]Declares War[/b], the initial War Support is based on their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] prior to the war. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORMAL_WAR_TOOLTIP]Formal Wars[/TIP] have no War Support penalty, and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SURPRISE_WAR_TOOLTIP]Surprise Wars[/TIP] have increased penalties for friendlier Relationships. Any time after a war begins, either leader can spend [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] to increase War Support. [nn]The leader with lower War Support suffers from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_WEARINESS_TOOLTIP]War Weariness[/TIP]. War Weariness causes reduced Combat Strength for all units as well as [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalties across all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Captured Settlements, especially those captured from someone you’re at war with, suffer increased [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalties. War Weariness stacks if you’re at war with more than one leader, and the penalties can add up very quickly. [nn]You can spend [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] to increase War Support, but it gets more expensive each time you do this. Other leaders can also choose to support or oppose your war, and other effects like [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP] bonuses, and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP] can all impact War Support.
Something To Try...

Don’t underestimate the importance of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP]. It can play a large role in how effective your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] are in battle and make the difference between defeating or losing a unit. [nn]If you’re declaring war, it is often worth taking the time to lower your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] first, so plan ahead. Consider saving up [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] to increase War Support early, giving your army a welcome boost to the initial fighting. If you find your empire is unhappy and you’re unable to reduce your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_WEARINESS_TOOLTIP]War Weariness[/TIP], it might be time to end the war.
Generating Science
Discovery relies on our Science output. For that, we need Science Buildings like Libraries and Observatories.

[icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] is a yield that advances your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech Tree[/TIP], unlocking the ability to construct [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], train more advanced units, and become more efficient. Progressing through the Tech Tree is also required to earn [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP] Points. [nn]Construct [b]Science Buildings[/b] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] to increase how much [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] you generate each turn. Improving certain tiles can also generate [b]Science[/b], as well as placing [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] once you unlock them. [nn]In addition, certain leaders can start the Research Collaboration Diplomatic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP], generating [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] for both parties. [nn]It’s important to generate a large amount of [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] if you want to win the Scientific Victory.
Something to try...

If you haven’t yet, research the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] [b]Writing[/b] then construct [b]Libraries[/b] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Place them near [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] to maximize their [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b]!
Generating Gold
The more Gold we earn, the more achievable our dreams. Try placing more Gold Buildings like Markets and Ports.

[icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] is a valuable yield used to expand and maintain your Empire. You can use it to directly purchase a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] or Unit if you don’t want to spend the time producing it. [nn]Construct Gold Buildings in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] to increase how much [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] you generate each turn. Improving certain tiles can also generate [b]Gold[/b]. Keep an eye on [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAINTENANCE_TOOLTIP]Maintenance[/TIP] costs for advanced Units and Buildings, though, as these cost [b]Gold[/b] each turn. [nn]In addition, certain leaders can start the Open Markets diplomatic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP], generating [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] for both parties. [nn]Finally, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] automatically convert all their [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] into [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b], so having a large number of productive Towns can be an excellent source of [b]Gold[/b]. [nn]As you generate [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b], it goes to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURY_TOOLTIP]Treasury[/TIP], which you can see at the top of your screen. Remember, [b]Gold[/b] in your Treasury is not doing anything useful, so be sure to put it to work!
Something to try...

If you haven’t yet, research the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] [b]Currency[/b], then construct [b]Markets[/b] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Be sure to place them near Coasts and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVIGABLE_RIVER_TOOLTIP]Navigable Rivers[/TIP] to maximize their [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] output!
Spending Gold
Gold exists to be spent. Treat yourself to that new Building or Unit you've had your eye on.

All the [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] we earn across our empire is added to our [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURY_TOOLTIP]Treasury[/TIP]. Once earned, we can immediately spend that [b]Gold[/b] on useful things. [nn]The most common use for [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] is [b]purchasing [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP][b] and Units[/b]. In fact, it’s the only way to construct Buildings and train Units in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] since only [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] can use their [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. [nn]When you purchase a Building, you immediately gain access to it and its benefits. When you purchase a Unit, the Unit is immediately trained, but it won’t be able to act until the next turn. Still, purchasing Units in this way can be a great way to provide a quick defense in a pinch! [nn]You can also purchase a Unit or Building that has been partially produced. In this case, the cost is reduced by however much progress has already been made. Note that you cannot purchase [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], so you still need to dedicate your [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] to them. [nn][b]Upgrading [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] is another common use of [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b]. When you unlock a new tier of a Unit via [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP], you can spend [b]Gold[/b] when an existing Unit is in your borders to upgrade it to the new tier. [nn][icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] has many more uses throughout your empire, like quickly repairing damaged tiles and [b]upgrading Towns to Cities[/b], so it’s important to have a healthy economy!
Something to try...

If you have some spare [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b], try purchasing your next Unit or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] rather than producing it. Click the Purchase tab on a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] and select an item to purchase it. Purchasing is the only option in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP], so you’ll need to spend [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] to build infrastructure or train Units there.
Relationships
Diplomacy, like war, requires strategy. Keep an eye on your Relationships with other Leaders.

Every leader has a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] level with all other leaders: Hostile, Unfriendly, Neutral, Friendly, or Helpful. These Relationships determine how likely the other leaders will accept or support your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP], what the penalty is for declaring a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SURPRISE_WAR_TOOLTIP]Surprise War[/TIP], and how likely they are to declare war on you. [nn]Relationships are improved by positive interactions, including shared Endeavors, mutual wars with a shared enemy, trade, sending aid, and other actions. Relationships are worsened by negative interactions, including [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SANCTION_TOOLTIP]Sanctions[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ESPIONAGE_TOOLTIP]Espionage[/TIP], encroaching on their desired territory, rejecting Endeavors, and more. All leaders have a unique Agenda that also impacts Relationships, and Relationships drift toward Neutral over time. [nn]When a Relationship reaches [b]Helpful[/b], you may request an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ALLIANCE_TOOLTIP]Alliance[/TIP]. There’s no guarantee the other side will agree, though. [nn]When a Relationship reaches [b]Hostile[/b], you can declare a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORMAL_WAR_TOOLTIP]Formal War[/TIP]. A Formal War has no [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] penalty, making it easier to fight. You can always ignore your diplomatic Relationship and declare a Surprise War, but there are steep penalties for doing so.
Something to try...

Pick a leader you already have a positive [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] with and try to get to Helpful with a combination of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP], trade, and meeting their Agenda. If there’s a leader you’d like to go to war with, consider using [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ESPIONAGE_TOOLTIP]Espionage[/TIP] actions or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SANCTION_TOOLTIP]Sanctions[/TIP] well in advance to lower your Relationship to Hostile before declaring war.
Cultural Victory
We will win the Cultural Victory if we attract the most Tourists to our empire. Let us conquer hearts, not cities.

There are four ways to achieve a victory in Civilization: Cultural, Military, Scientific, and Economic. The first leader that achieves any of these victories wins the game. [nn]To win a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP], you must attract [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourists[/TIP] to your empire. Tourists are a measure of how attractive your empire is to others. All sorts of things can attract Tourists, including constructing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] and your civilization’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP]. [nn]Having [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP] within your borders also provides Tourists, as does each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebration[/TIP] you achieve and some [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Works[/TIP] you display. You’ll even get Tourists if you study Future [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic[/TIP] at the end of the Civics Tree! [nn]Basically, you need to build the kind of empire somebody would want to visit. [nn]To see your [b]Tourist Score[/b] and how you rank against the other leaders, visit the [b]Victory Panel[/b]. As the game progresses, you’ll see the number of points required to win the game. It’s not possible to win a Cultural Victory in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], so you’ll learn more about that later.
Keep this in mind…

In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], look for opportunities to settle near [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP] and construct Antiquity Age [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP]. Having these in your empire is a great start toward achieving a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP].
Generating Culture
Tourism and beauty thrive only if we can create enough Culture.

[icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] is a yield that advances your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics Trees[/TIP], unlocking [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SOCIAL_POLICY_TOOLTIP]Social Policies[/TIP] that shape your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GOVERNMENT_TOOLTIP]Government[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] with powerful effects, and more. [nn]Construct [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b][b] [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] to increase how much [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] you generate each turn. Settling near [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP] and improving certain tiles can also generate [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b]. [nn]In addition, certain leaders can start the [b]Cultural Exchange[/b] diplomatic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP], generating [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] for both parties. [nn]It’s important to generate a large amount of [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] if you want to win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP].
Something to try…

If you haven't yet, research the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] [b]Masonry[/b] then construct [b]Monuments[/b] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. Place them near a Mountain, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonder[/TIP], or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonder[/TIP] to maximize their [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] yields!
Unique Civics
By researching our Unique Civics, we can discover what only we can create.

Every Civilization has [b]Unique [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP] that unlock powerful effects to enhance that Civilization's strengths. [nn]During a Civilization's [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_APEX_AGE_TOOLTIP]Apex Age[/TIP], additional effects, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Unique Units[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP], and more can be unlocked via these Unique Civics to help that Civilization truly shine. Be sure to take advantage of these while available. [nn]Outside the Apex Age, you can still find important effects that shape your people, including the ability to adopt the ways of other Civilizations to make something truly unique!
Something to try…
Research a Unique [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic[/TIP] to unlock a special bonus. These are the Civics found under your Civilization’s Civics Tree or the Time Tested Civics Tree.
Increase Production
Wonders can create a lasting cultural impact on the world. Let us ensure we have the means to produce them.

Since each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonder[/TIP] is unique, only one Civilization can complete it per game. Before you begin [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] one, you need to make sure your [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] is up to the task. [nn][icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] is a yield that determines how quickly a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] can construct a Building, [b]Unit[/b], or Wonder. You can increase your [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] with improved tiles, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouse[/TIP] Buildings, and Production Buildings. [nn]Managing [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] is an important skill in the game. If producing items is taking too long, you may need to invest further in [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b].
Something to try…

Your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP] is the best place to start. As it [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grows[/TIP] in Population, improve tiles with high [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. Find a [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouse[/TIP][b] [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP], like a [b]Harbor[/b] or [b]Brickyard[/b], that best matches your Capital’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP] and construct it. [nn]Later when you unlock the [b]Barracks[/b] and then [b]Blacksmith[/b], build those to further propel your [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. If you place them adjacent to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], they’ll have even higher yields!
Wonders
Wonders can both inspire our people and make us the envy of our neighbors, but we must build them before others can.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] are special constructibles with permanent, powerful effects. While [b]Cultural Civilizations[/b] will seek them out, they can be useful for many different playstyles. Explore the different Wonders to find one that interests you. [nn]Each Wonder can only be completed once in the world. If another player beats you to a Wonder while you're constructing it, you'll stop [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] it, and the spent [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] will be automatically applied to the next thing your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] builds. [nn]If another leader beats you to a Wonder you want, perhaps your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Military Advisor[/TIP] has ideas on how to acquire it through other means...
Next steps...

Choose a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonder[/TIP] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP]’s [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] list to begin constructing it. If none are available, study a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic[/TIP] or research a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP] to unlock one. Your Civilization’s associated Wonder is a good place to start, but any Wonder with an effect useful to you is worth pursuing. [nn]Note that some Wonders have specific placement requirements, limiting where they can be built. Once a Wonder is built, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP] cannot be built atop of it, even in later [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Ages[/TIP]. Don’t let that stop you – Wonders are always good to have.
Towns and Cities
With Cities to build Wonders and Towns to feed the people, our empire can be a place of grandeur and beauty.

Newly settled [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] start as [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP]. You can purchase [b]Units[/b] and basic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] in Towns with [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b], but they have no [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] queue. [nn]Towns are very helpful for your empire. They can secure strategic locations and gain access to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP]. All of a Town's [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] is converted to [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b], and eventually Towns can send [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] and specialize to provide powerful bonuses to your empire. [nn]Cities, like your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP], are more advanced Settlements that can use their [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] to train Units and construct advanced Buildings and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]. You can convert a Town to a City for a [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] cost, allowing access to its [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. [nn]You’ll always want some Towns because they provide boosts to [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] and [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b], but Cities have access to more powerful Buildings and Wonders. Maintaining a balance between Towns and Cities is an important skill in the game.
When you're ready...

To convert a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP], select it and choose [b]Convert to City[/b] at the bottom of the [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] list. It will instantly become a City, allowing it to produce advanced [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], and more. The [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] cost will depend on the Town’s size and other factors.
Natural Wonders
Few, if any, can rival Nature herself in the creation of beauty. But if we settle near Natural Wonders, we could be their stewards.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP] are terrain features of exceptional beauty that can be found scattered across the map. Keep an eye out for them while your [b]Scout[/b] explores the area around your starting location. You can identify a Natural Wonder by the unique map feature, and hovering the tile will provide both its name and unique effect. [nn]Once found, consider settling a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] near the Natural Wonder to claim it as your own. Be sure to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP] your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] quickly to bring the Natural Wonder within your borders. [nn]Once you improve a Natural Wonder tile, you’ll gain its special effects and also get a large number of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourists[/TIP] added to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP] score. Be sure to defend this Settlement, though, because other leaders may want to claim it as their own! [nn]Later, you can consider specializing this Town into a [b]Resort Town[/b] for an even bigger boost of yields and [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b]!
Thinking ahead...

Use a [b]Scout[/b] to find a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonder[/TIP] near your empire. If it appears to be unclaimed and in a defensible location, consider sending a [b]Settler[/b] to found a new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] within three tiles of the Natural Wonder. As the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grows[/TIP], be sure to improve the [b]Natural Wonder’s[/b] tiles.
Unique Improvements
With our Unique Improvements, we can enrich our lands and create Tourism.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP] are special [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RURAL_TOOLTIP]Rural[/TIP] tiles that provide additional bonuses on top of the standard [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP], like Farms and Mines. In order to construct a Unique Improvement, you must have access to one either through your [b]Civilization[/b] or a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP] you [b]Befriended[/b]. [nn]Unique Improvements are special because they do not remove the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouse[/TIP][b] Bonus[/b] of the tile they’re constructed on. For example, if an Emporium is constructed over a Farm, you’ll receive [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] from the Emporium, the bonus [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] from the Granary, as well as any of the standard yields the tile provides from being improved. [nn]Every Unique Improvement has placement restrictions. Some may only be built once in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP], but others can be built multiple times. When [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] multiple instances of the same Unique Improvement in a Settlement, you may need to invest more [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] or [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. [nn]Unique Improvements also provide [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP] for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP], so be sure to build as many as you can if you’re going after that victory!
Something to try...

If your Civilization provides access to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvement[/TIP], study the [b]Unique [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic[/TIP] that unlocks it. Otherwise, befriend an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Power[/TIP] and choose the [b]Unique Improvement [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP][b] Bonus[/b] when complete. Once you have access to a Unique Improvement, you can construct it in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] or City that meets the requirements.
Celebrations
When our people are happiest, we draw the attention of the whole world. Each Celebration we have contributes to our Tourism.

Each turn, every point of excess [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] across your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] goes toward your next [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebration[/TIP]. When enough [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] is accrued, your empire starts a Celebration, giving you a choice between strong bonuses based on your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GOVERNMENT_TOOLTIP]Government[/TIP]. Every time a Celebration begins, you also gain a new [b]Policy[/b] slot. [nn]Every point of excess [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] drives toward your next Celebration, so look for opportunities to increase [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b]. Watch out for [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP][b] [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAINTENANCE_TOOLTIP]Maintenance[/TIP] and going over your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_LIMIT_TOOLTIP]Settlement Limit[/TIP], because both of those can decrease your [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b]. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_WEARINESS_TOOLTIP]War Weariness[/TIP] can also decrease [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] while you’re at War, so try to make peace quickly! [nn]Celebrations add [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP] each time they begin after Researching Entertainment, so they’re a great way to secure extra points for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP]. Maintaining high [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] is an important skill to master if you’re going after the Cultural Victory.
Keep in mind...

[b]Mysticism[/b] unlocks the [b]Altar[/b] for an early [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP], and [b]Military Training[/b] unlocks the [b]Arena[/b] for a big boost. Look for [b]Policies[/b] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADITION_TOOLTIP]Traditions[/TIP] that boost [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b], as well as certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], Narrative Events, and tiles with high [b]Appeal[/b]
Cultural Victory Scoring
An empire is a unique tapestry of people, places, and ideas. The greater our tapestry, the more Tourism we attract.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they achieve cultural dominance against all other leaders. This dominance is measured by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP] and comes from the following sources: [nn]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP]: 10 points when at least one tile is improved [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]: 4 points in Antiquity, 8 points in Exploration, and 12 points in Modern [n]- [b]Displayed [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIC_TOOLTIP]Relics[/TIP]: 3 points [n]- [b]Displayed [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ARTIFACT_TOOLTIP]Artifacts[/TIP]: 5 points [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebrations[/TIP]: 2 points per [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] after Researching Entertainment [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP]: 1 point for every type of Unique Improvement in a Settlement (4 points in Settlements connected by Rail after Researching Industrialization's Mastery in the Modern Age) [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP]: 1 point in Antiquity, 2 points in Exploration, and 4 points in Modern (7 points in Settlements with an Aerodrome after Researching Flight's Mastery) [n]- [b]Resort [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP]: 4 points per Breathtaking tile when at least 7 tiles are Breathtaking after Researching Globalism's Mastery [n]- [b]Certain [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP][b] and [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP]: Varies [nn]Note that Wonders captured from other leaders are worth greatly reduced points. [nn]Starting in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], a winner is declared if the first place leader has 6x the points of the second place leader. As time goes on, that requirement lowers until only 1.25x is required toward the end of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP]. See the Victory screen for more information.
Keep in Mind...

There are many ways to win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP], but the bottom line is you need to earn more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP] than your opponents! Look for opportunities to gain points and deny others from earning them. As time goes on, the amount you need to dominate other leaders is reduced, making victory more achievable.
Cultural Endeavors
Endeavors provide helpful bonuses like additional Culture, as well as improve relationships with other Leaders.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP] are diplomatic efforts between two leaders that can provide a bonus for both sides. An Endeavor begins when one leader spends [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] to propose a specific Endeavor with another. That leader can then choose to Accept, Support, or Reject the Endeavor. [nn]Accepting an Endeavor is free and provides a moderate boost to the proposer and a small boost to the acceptor. Supporting an Endeavor costs [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b], provides the strongest boost to both sides, and increases your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP]. Rejecting an Endeavor costs [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b], cancels the Endeavor, decreases your Relationship, and blocks further Endeavors for several turns. [nn]There are many different Endeavors in the game. Some are unlocked by your leader’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attribute[/TIP] types and others are unlocked by studying [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], befriending [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP], and more. [nn]Endeavors are a powerful way to maintain friendly diplomatic relations while receiving useful bonuses. They’re a great way to spend your [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] and can significantly boost your empire.
Something to try...

If you are a leader with the [b]Cultural [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attribute[/TIP], you will have access to the [b]Cultural Exchange [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP]. Open the Diplomacy screen of a leader and select Cultural Exchange under the Endeavors. This will cost [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] whether or not the other leader agrees, so it’s better to choose a leader you have a strong [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] with. [nn]If you don’t have access to Cultural Exchange, other Endeavors can still be helpful toward your victory. Consider making friends with a [b]Cultural Leader[/b] to encourage them to start a Cultural Exchange with you.
Triumph: Wonders of the Ancient World
Our Wonders bring such beauty to our empire. Let us see much beauty we can create!

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] are special, optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. The Cultural Triumphs are a good match if you’re pursuing a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP]. [nn]There are two types of Triumphs. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age. [nn]You can only select three Dedications at the start of each Age, though, so keep that in mind as you pursue them. [nn]Triumphs can provide extra challenges and reward playstyles different from the ones you may normally try. When you’re ready to push yourself, give them a shot!
Something to try...

You can find the list of all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] and your progress toward them in your empire’s Legacy screen. Look through the different challenges and rewards to decide if you want to pursue any. Use the Track feature if you want to keep track of your progress in the game’s UI. [nn][b]The [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP][b] of the Ancient World[/b] is a good Triumph to target when you’re aiming for a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP]. It’s a tough challenge, and it may take you a few games to accomplish it.
Military Victory
By controlling the most Settlements, we bring the world under our empire’s protection. This is the path to the Military Victory.

There are four ways to achieve a victory in Civilization: Cultural, Military, Scientific, and Economic. The first leader that achieves any of these victories wins the game. [nn]To win a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP], you must control the most [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] while navigating a dangerous world. It’s actually quite simple. If you find unclaimed land, settle it. If you find claimed land, conquer it. There’s more to it than that, but for now your focus is on expanding your territory to increase your [b]Dominion Score[/b]. [nn]To see your Dominion Score and how you rank against the other leaders, visit the [b]Victory Panel[/b]. As the game progresses, you’ll see the number of points required to win the game. It’s not possible to win in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], so you’ll learn more about it later.
Keep this in mind…

In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], look for opportunities to settle in defensible or strategically important locations. Also don’t be afraid to “forward settle” or settle a new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] near your opponents. It will decrease your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] with them, but you’re likely to go to war with them anyway.
Training Units
Threat – or opportunity – can come at any time. Training Military Units will help us prepare for both.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] are the fighting forces you can use both to defend your Civilization and to wage war against others. [nn]There are several types of Military Units. [b]Infantry[/b] units are melee combatants and [b]Ranged[/b] units can attack from a distance but are weak when defending. Other types can be unlocked over time by researching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP]. [nn]Units can be trained in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] using [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. They can also be purchased instantly with [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] from any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP], which is useful if a Settlement is under threat. [nn]Keep in mind that most Military Units have a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAINTENANCE_TOOLTIP]Maintenance[/TIP] cost of some amount of [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] per turn, so a large military requires a strong economy.
Something to try…

In any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP], produce a few [b]Warriors[/b], [b]Slingers[/b], or some other [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP]. To instantly purchase a unit, click the Purchase tab in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]’s [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] menu and select the unit if you have enough [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b]. Remember, you can only purchase one unit per turn per Settlement no matter how much [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] you have.
Independent Powers
Hostile Independent Powers are liable to become a nuisance if left unchecked. Let's deal with them before that happens.

Often the earliest danger is a nearby [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Power[/TIP]. Hostile Independent Powers, outlined with red, may send raiding parties to attack your people. These raiding parties are a nuisance at best and a real threat at worst. [nn]Having [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] defend your empire is a good first step, but to put an end to their attacks, you’ll need to address the source. First, you need to find where they’re coming from. A Scout is a useful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUPPORT_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Support Unit[/TIP] that helps you map out the area surrounding your empire. [nn]Once you find the Independent Power, you have two choices: befriend them or disperse them. Befriending them requires a large amount of [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b], and once several turns have elapsed, they’ll no longer be hostile. Eventually, they may even turn into a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP] and name you [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP], providing you with a strong bonus for the rest of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. [nn]The other option is to disperse them. This requires sending a Military Unit onto the Independent Power’s village, which usually means defeating their military. Dispersing an Independent Power rewards you with a large amount of its associated yield as a one-time bonus.
Something to try...

Locate a [b]hostile [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Power[/TIP] and use your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] to defeat theirs. Once the Independent Power’s village is exposed, move any Military Unit on it and select [b]Disperse[/b] Independent Power from the unit’s action panel. Note that you can use this action even when the unit has no movement left!
Army Commanders
Our Armies need Commanders to lead them. Even the sharpest sword is useless without a strong hand to wield it.

[b]Army [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commanders[/TIP] are [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUPPORT_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Support Units[/TIP] that have special abilities and provide bonuses to nearby [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP]. Army Commanders also have the ability to [b]pack Military Units[/b] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVILIAN_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Civilian Units[/TIP], allowing them to quickly transport them across the map. [nn]Army Commanders gain [b]XP[/b] any time combat occurs within their[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMAND_RADIUS_TOOLTIP]Command Radius[/TIP][/b]. As they level up, they receive [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotions[/TIP], granting them further bonuses and abilities. Any time an Army Commander receives the final Promotion in a path, a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMENDATION_TOOLTIP]Commendation[/TIP] becomes available. Leveled up Army Commanders can make a very big difference in the outcome of a war, so be sure to keep your Army Commanders on the front line where the action is. [nn]When a unit is adjacent to an Army Commander, they can be packed inside the Commander using the [b]Add to Army[/b] (on the Unit) or [b]Assemble Army[/b] (on the Commander) commands. Commanders can have up to four units packed at a time, and additional capacity can be unlocked via Promotions. Once packed, the units travel with the Army Commander, and they can be [b]Deployed[/b] together or one at a time to rejoin the battlefield. [nn]Finally, if your Army Commander is defeated in combat, it will automatically respawn a few turns later in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP].
Something to try...

If you haven’t yet, study the [b]Discipline [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic[/TIP] to gain a free Army [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP]. Bring several units and your Commander together and use the [b]Assemble Army[/b] command to pack them. From there, move your army across the battlefield toward a hostile unit or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Power[/TIP]. [b]Deploy[/b] the units and attack, earning XP until your Commander earns a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotion[/TIP]. [nn]If in doubt for which Promotion to choose, Assault is a good first choice.
Settling
Settlers can establish new Towns, extending our reach and visibility without unnecessary bloodshed.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] are the lifeblood of your empire, serving as the hubs for generating yields, producing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] and units, collecting [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], growing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP], and claiming territory. [nn]Settlements are founded by [b]Settler[/b] units, which can be trained in any Settlement with at least 5 Population. Once trained, Settlers need to move to the tile where you wish to found the new Settlement. As [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVILIAN_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Civilian Units[/TIP], Settlers are vulnerable to attack, so be sure to protect them with your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP]! [nn]Choosing where to settle is as much an art as it is a science and depends greatly on your current situation and goals. The Settler lens can help identify which locations are possible and which are even recommended. In general, look for locations with strong yields, a large number of nearby Resources, defensible tiles, and strategic locations. [nn]Be sure to consider your neighbors, too! Other leaders dislike it when you settle too close to their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP], and having borders that touch increases tensions. Neutral [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_INDEPENDENT_POWER_TOOLTIP]Independent Powers[/TIP] will turn hostile if you settle too close, and you’ll need to immediately defend the vulnerable new Settlement.
Something to try...

Use the Settler Lens in the Lens Toggles menu to find a suitable location to expand. Once your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP] reaches 5 [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP], train a Settler unit and send them to that location. Be sure to keep the Settler safe on its journey with [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP]. Once it arrives, use the Settler to found a new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP].
Declaring War
Another Leader is Hostile toward us. If we are to Declare War, now is the time to do it.

Any leader can declare war on any other leader. If the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] is anything but [b]Hostile[/b], this is considered a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SURPRISE_WAR_TOOLTIP]Surprise War[/TIP], and the aggressor takes a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] penalty based on how friendly the Relationship was. If the Relationship is Hostile, this is considered a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORMAL_WAR_TOOLTIP]Formal War[/TIP] and there is no War Support penalty. [nn]The primary outcome of War is that [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] on the opposing sides can attack one another, enter each others’ borders, and capture [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. In addition, all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavors[/TIP] immediately end. [nn][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerained[/TIP] by either side automatically join the war, and any Allies must immediately make a choice to either join the war or end the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ALLIANCE_TOOLTIP]Alliance[/TIP]. Allies who enter a Joint War in this way do not suffer War Support regardless of Relationship. [nn]Once a War is declared, it continues for a minimum of 10 turns. After that point, either side can Propose Peace, but the war will not end until an agreement is made.
Keep in Mind...

To be the most prepared for declaring war, ensure your military is strong and well-positioned, you have a hostile [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_TOOLTIP]Relationship[/TIP] with the opposing leader, and you’re aware of any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ALLIANCE_TOOLTIP]Alliances[/TIP] they have or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP] that may support them. [nn]Watch your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP] carefully, because it can have a large impact on the effectiveness of your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] and empire!
Capturing Settlements
Settlements are well-guarded these days. We'll only take them if we occupy all of their Fortifications.

While at war, you can capture the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] of your enemies, giving you control of that Settlement along with all of its territory, yields, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], and more. This can be a great way to strengthen your empire or weaken an enemy’s, and it’s a key component of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP]. [nn]In order to capture a Settlement, you must destroy any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEFENSIVE_FORTIFICATION_TOOLTIP]Defensive Fortifications[/TIP] of the Settlement and have a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Unit[/TIP] occupy those tiles. Once occupied, the tile remains occupied until another leader’s Military Unit occupies that tile, making it risky to leave the tile undefended if other forces are nearby. Be aware that in joint wars, the leader that claims the final tile is awarded the Settlement! [nn]Once a Settlement is captured, you’ll have the option to [b]Keep or Raze[/b] the Settlement. Keeping it puts the Settlement in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNREST_TOOLTIP]Unrest[/TIP] for 10 turns, limiting your ability to control it until the Unrest is complete. Alternately, Razing the Settlement will reduce its [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP] one turn at a time until the Settlement is permanently destroyed. [nn]If you capture a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP], you will immediately remove the City-State and their units from the game. Use this tactic against leaders with many City-States under their control. [nn]Captured Settlements still count against your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_LIMIT_TOOLTIP]Settlement Limit[/TIP], including Settlements you are in the process of Razing. Be sure your empire can support the new Settlement and that it provides enough value to keep.
Keep in Mind...

Capturing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] can be a great way to get ahead. In fact, it may be the only way to gain access to key territory or a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonder[/TIP] that another leader beat you to. It can also be a great way to punish an enemy who foolishly attacked you. If you’re pursuing the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP], it’s nearly inescapable that you’ll need to capture Settlements in order to win. [nn]Consider the costs and risks for capturing Settlements. Your empire can only [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP] so large so quickly, and a rapidly expanding empire can quickly fall victim to [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] issues. Smart leaders understand that not every Settlement you capture is worth keeping…
Combat Strength
Before you engage the enemy, be aware of your Units' Combat Strength. Not every Unit is suited for every situation.

When a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Unit[/TIP] attacks, damage is based on the difference in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] between the two units. Combat Strength is derived from many factors, including the unit’s base strength, the terrain it occupies, any bonuses or penalties on the unit, nearby [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commanders[/TIP], and the unit’s current health. [nn][b]Infantry[/b] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAVALRY_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Cavalry[/TIP] units take [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RECIPROCAL_DAMAGE_TOOLTIP]Reciprocal Damage[/TIP] when they attack, meaning they lose health based on the Combat Strength of the defender. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RANGED_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Ranged Units[/TIP], on the other hand, safely attack from a distance, but they’re vulnerable to being attacked. It’s often better to first soften an enemy unit with Ranged Units before sending in the Infantry or Cavalry, but be sure you don’t leave your Ranged Units exposed! [nn]Your Commanders are also an important source of Combat Strength. As they level up, they can provide bonuses to nearby units for different situations. You can also increase Combat Strength by studying specific [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP], having access to certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMPIRE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Empire Resources[/TIP], becoming [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP] of [b]Military [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP], having positive [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_SUPPORT_TOOLTIP]War Support[/TIP], and through the [b]Military Aid [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP]. [nn]Remember, each bit of Combat Strength can add up to make a big difference during battle.
Something To Try...

Before confirming an attack, pay attention to the battle preview information. It will tell you why each side is gaining various bonuses and penalties. Use this information to maximize the effectiveness of your units. [nn]Pay particular attention to any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Unique Units[/TIP] you have access to either through your civilization’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_APEX_AGE_TOOLTIP]Apex Age[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SYNCRETISM_TOOLTIP]Syncretism[/TIP]. Unique Units often have special effects that give them bonuses under certain conditions. Maximizing these effects can be a powerful way to gain an edge on the battlefield. [nn]Improve [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] like Horses and Iron or gain access via [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] to provide a bonus to certain unit types. Use your [icon:YIELD_DIPLOMACY][b]Influence[/b] to become [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP] of a Military [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP] or, if your leader has access to it, start a Military Aid [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP].
Terrain Tactics
Position your Units on terrain that offers defensive bonuses, and take heed of tiles that stop movement.

Terrain plays a key role in battle. Different terrain types can provide bonuses or penalties to attackers and defenders. For example, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ROUGH_TERRAIN_TOOLTIP]Rough Terrain[/TIP] tiles provide a bonus when defending and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_RIVER_TOOLTIP]Minor River[/TIP] tiles provide a penalty when attacking. [nn]Terrain can also drive how units are positioned. Rough, [b]Vegetated[/b], and Minor River tiles end movement, slowing how units advance or retreat. Any tiles that block vision, like Vegetated and Mountainous tiles, also prevent [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RANGED_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Ranged Units[/TIP] from attacking past them, so keep that in mind when positioning units like Archers. [nn]Taking advantage of terrain can make a real difference. Forcing the enemy to cross [b]Marine[/b] tiles or positioning Ranged Units on [b]Cliffs[/b] can make short work of a passing army. Chokepoints formed by impassable terrain, like Mountainous tiles, are much easier to defend than open Flat lands. Preparations before a war, like where to settle a new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] or place [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEFENSIVE_FORTIFICATION_TOOLTIP]Defensive Fortifications[/TIP], can have a lasting impact on your ability to defend. [nn]Finally, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotions[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Unique Units[/TIP], leader or civilization abilities, Mementos, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], and other effects can affect how your units interact with the terrain. Strategically taking advantage of your strengths is an important part of battle!
Something To Try...

When attacking or defending, analyze the terrain of the battlefield. Consider where each unit can make the best use of the terrain, and pay attention to if a tile will cause movement to end prematurely. Before moving [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RANGED_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Ranged Units[/TIP], consider whether or not their vision will be blocked. [nn]If possible, try to force the enemy to cross Marine tiles or waste turns going around impassable terrain. Set up a strong defense by [b]Fortifying[/b] units on terrain that provides defensive bonuses and can’t be reached by Ranged Units.
Military Victory Scoring
Every Settlement we control is valuable for the Military Victory, but some are worth more Dominion than others.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they achieve military dominance against all other leaders. This dominance is measured by Dominion Points and are primarily a measure of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP]. [nn]Each Settlement you control is worth 4 points. Settlements can be worth additional points as follows: [n]- [b]Original [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CAPITAL_TOOLTIP]Capital[/TIP]: +4 points [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP]: +1 point [n]- [b]Captured[/b]: +1 point [n]- [b]Captured from Ideological Opponent[/b]: +2 points [nn]Starting in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], a winner is declared if the first place leader has 6x the points of the second place leader. As time goes on, that requirement lowers until only 1.25x is required toward the end of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP]. See the [b]Victory Screen[/b] for more information.
Keep in mind...

There are many ways to win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP], but the bottom line is you need to have more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] than your opponents. Look for opportunities to settle new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP], but more importantly, look for valuable Settlements you can capture from your opponents!
Triumph: Pax Imperatoria
If we keep capturing Settlements, we'll be well on our way to claiming the Pax Imperatoria Triumph.
