[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] are special, optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. The Military Triumphs are a good match if you’re pursuing a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP]. [nn]There are two types of Triumphs. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age. You can only select a limited number of Dedications at the start of each Age, though, so keep that in mind as you pursue them. [nn]Triumphs can provide extra challenges and reward playstyles different from the ones you may normally try. When you’re ready to push yourself, give them a shot!
Something To Try...

You can find the list of all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] and your progress toward them in your empire’s Legacy screen. Look through the different challenges and rewards to decide if you want to pursue any. Use the Track feature if you want to keep track of your progress in the game’s UI. [nn][b]Pax Imperatoria[/b] is a good Triumph to target when you’re aiming for a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP]. It’s a tough challenge, and it may take you a few games to accomplish it.
Scouting
Intelligence is the foundation of an effective strategy. Deploy a few Scouts to see what's beyond our borders.

Scouting is the act of exploring your surroundings and having visibility into what’s occurring in the world. This visibility allows you to act quickly and prepare for threats or react to opportunities before your opponents can. [nn]Scouts are a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUPPORT_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Support Unit[/TIP] that’s available at the very start of the game. While all Units are capable of revealing the map and providing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SIGHT_TOOLTIP]Sight[/TIP], Scouts are particularly good at it. Their Search ability allows them to see in a large area around them without moving, and they’re able to detect [b]Discoveries[/b] from an even farther distance. Using this ability often can help you reach Discoveries before others, providing important bonuses early in the game. For this reason, Scouts are often an excellent choice for the first Unit to train. [nn]Scouts are also capable of Auto Exploration. When enabled, the Scout will automatically explore unexplored areas, revealing the map for you without requiring micro management. If the Scout comes upon a Discovery or hostile enemy, the Scout will alert you and ask for a command. [nn]While Scouts can’t attack other Units, they can provide useful information during battles. By scouting ahead of your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP], you can learn valuable information about how and where your opponent is deploying their Units.
Something to try...

Train a Scout and have them explore the surroundings. Use the Search ability to quickly find Discoveries before your opponents do. Once you’ve mapped out your surrounding area, use the Auto Explore ability to have the Scout continue to explore automatically. [nn]Scouting is so important that it’s often wise to have several Scouts exploring the world and keeping tabs on your opponents, especially early in the game.
Scientific Victory
To win the Space Race...I can think of no better proof of our empire’s greatness. We have much to accomplish.

There are four ways to achieve a victory in Civilization: Cultural, Military, Scientific, and Economic. The first leader that achieves any of these victories wins the game. [nn]To win a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP], you must win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPACE_RACE_TOOLTIP]Space Race[/TIP]. As you achieve scientific milestones, you’ll earn [b]Innovation[/b]. Once you reach 100 Innovation while controlling an active Launch Pad for 10 turns, you’ll achieve the Scientific Victory. [nn]Innovation is earned through a variety of means, including [b]Antiquity [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENCE_PROJECT_TOOLTIP]Science Projects[/TIP]. Your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Science Advisor[/TIP] will give you details on how to earn these as the game progresses. [nn]To see your [b]Innovation Score[/b] and how you rank against the other leaders in the race, visit the [b]Victory Panel[/b]. It’s not possible to win the game during Antiquity, but having a strong start going into the next [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] is always helpful.
Keep this in mind...

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP] is truly a race against the other leaders in all victory types. As you’re progressing, be aware of how your opponents are doing in the other victory types. The key to a Scientific Victory is reaching the finish line before anyone else is able to dominate in military, [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b], or economy.
Tech Masteries
Technology Masteries provide a variety of benefits we would be wise not to ignore.

[b]Technologies[/b] have [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Mastery[/TIP] nodes that can be researched after the main [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] is completed. This represents studying further into that Tech, providing additional related bonuses. These are optional, and you should only spend the time researching them if you'll take advantage of the bonuses. [nn]Some [b]Masteries[/b] provide [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP][b] Points[/b], so if you’re going for a Scientific Victory, these can be worth pursuing.
Something to try...

If you haven’t yet, research the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] Writing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Mastery[/TIP]. This Mastery provides a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codex[/TIP] you can slot and an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ESPIONAGE_TOOLTIP]Espionage[/TIP] action that lets you steal Technologies from other leaders.
Codices
Whenever we make a discovery, we create a Great Work called a Codex. But Codices are only valuable if we enshrine them in Buildings.

A [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codex[/TIP] is a scientific [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Work[/TIP] produced through various means. Once produced, Codices can be slotted into any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] with a [b]Great Work Slot[/b] to provide bonus [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b], [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP] Points. [nn]The primary way to produce a Codex is via [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP]. They can also be produced when studying certain Civic Masteries, becoming [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP] of Scientific [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP], and by constructing certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]. [nn]Codices must be slotted to grant bonus [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] and [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b]. In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], [b]Libraries[/b], [b]Academies[/b], and certain Wonders all grant [b]Great Work Slots[/b]. Be sure to construct enough Buildings with slots to take full advantage of your Codices!
Something to try...

If you haven’t yet, research the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Technology[/TIP] Writing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Mastery[/TIP]. This Mastery provides a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codex[/TIP], which will automatically slot into an empty [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Work[/TIP] Slot when complete. You can manage your Great Works in the Great Works Screen.
Adjacency Bonuses
Buildings earn additional yields whenever placed adjacent to features like Mountains or Resources. And when adjacent to more than one? Now that’s efficiency!

Many [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] provide [b]Adjacency Bonuses[/b], or increased yields based on what tiles are adjacent to it. For example, [b]Libraries[/b] receive extra [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] if placed next to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]. When constructing a new Building, pay attention to the Building's Adjacency Bonuses and look for locations that provide the highest yields. [nn]Most non-[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouse[/TIP] Buildings receive an adjacency for Wonders. Generally, these Buildings will also receive an adjacency based on the Building’s type: [n]- [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] and Production Buildings: Resources [n]- [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b] and Happiness Buildings: Mountains and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP] [n]- [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] and Gold Buildings: Coastal Tiles and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVIGABLE_RIVER_TOOLTIP]Navigable Rivers[/TIP] [nn]In addition, [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] increase the benefit of your Adjacency bonuses, adding another way to further enhance the yields of your tiles. Specialists require extra [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] and [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b], so be careful to place them well.
Keep in Mind…

Sometimes you'll need to plan ahead to unlock the highest bonuses. New Urban [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]Districts[/TIP] must be [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONNECTED_TOOLTIP]Connected[/TIP] to another Urban District in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP], so you may need to construct some [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] before you reach that perfect location. [nn]Thinking through the best locations for your different Building types is an important skill for getting the most out of your Buildings. The details panel shown while placing Buildings can help you understand how the yields are calculated.
Specialists
The next time a City grows, place a Specialist on an Urban District instead of placing a Rural Improvement to watch your yields soar!

Each time a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grows[/TIP], you have the option to assign that Population to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RURAL_TOOLTIP]Rural[/TIP] tile, creating an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvement[/TIP] like a Mine or Farm, or to an Urban [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]District[/TIP]. When assigned to an Urban District, the Population becomes a [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialist[/TIP]. [nn][icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] act as Adjacency Bonus enhancers. Each Specialist placed on a District provides the full Adjacency Bonus for all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] in that District. This can add up to very powerful yields! [nn][icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] can only be placed in Cities, and there’s a limit to the maximum number of [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] you can place on a single tile, represented by the circular pips during a [b]Growth Event[/b]. As you progress through the game, that limit can be increased. [nn]Each [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialist[/TIP] has a [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b][b] and [/b][icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b][b] [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAINTENANCE_TOOLTIP]Maintenance[/TIP][b] cost[/b], which increases with each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Before placing a [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialist[/TIP], make sure that you have enough [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] to keep your citizens happy!
Something to Try…

When a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP]’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP] Grows, weigh the pros and cons of creating a [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialist[/TIP] versus creating an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvement[/TIP]. If you’ve already grabbed key [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], expanded your borders, and built some [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], it may be time for a Specialist. Don’t forget to confirm that you can afford the [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] penalty. The penalty for going unhappy is probably worse than the bonus the Specialist provides. [nn]Knowing when to place Specialists and managing the balance between Urban [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]Districts[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RURAL_TOOLTIP]Rural[/TIP] tiles is a key skill for the game. Don’t be afraid to experiment!
Projects
Projects can keep a City productive when no new Buildings or Units are needed. Some Projects even award Innovation.

In addition to training Units and constructing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] can produce [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP]. A Project is a task that provides a special benefit either while being produced or after it’s completed. [nn]The two most common Projects are Research Initiative and Cultural Festival. These Projects provide the associated yield each turn they’re produced, providing a great way to spend excess [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] to boost [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] or [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b]. [nn]As you progress through the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech Tree[/TIP], you’ll unlock more Projects. Several Projects, like Chart the Stars, provide large amounts of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP] Points. If you’re going for a Scientific Victory, it’s important that you unlock and complete them. Even if you’re not focused on a Scientific Victory, they can provide other bonuses like [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attribute[/TIP] Points or free Buildings or Units.
Keep in Mind…

It’s often not recommended to build every [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP], and you don’t want to produce more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] than your economy can afford. Spending time on [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP] is a great way to spend a City’s [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] when other needs are met!
Scientific Victory Scoring
To win the Space Race, we must seize every opportunity to gain Innovation.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPACE_RACE_TOOLTIP]Space Race[/TIP]. This requires earning 100 Innovation and having an active Launch Pad. [nn][b]Innovation[/b] are earned through many different ways. The two primary ways to earn them are by researching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP] and completing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP]. You can unlock these Projects by researching advanced [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Techs[/TIP] in each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], then you can produce them in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] that meets the requirements. The Masteries and Projects vary in point values. [nn]Certain Science-based [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] provide 3 points, and you can earn an additional 1 point for each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CODEX_TOOLTIP]Codex[/TIP] displayed in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Work[/TIP][b] Slot[/b] during the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP]. Some [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP] also provide Innovation. [nn]The Scientific Victory can only be won in the Modern Age since it requires [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] a Launch Pad. The first leader that reaches 100 Innovation with an active Launch Pad will win the game after a short countdown. See the [b]Victory Screen[/b] for more information.
Keep in Mind…

There are many ways to win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP], but the bottom line is that you first need to earn 100 Innovation. Look for opportunities to study the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP] that reward points, and unlock [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENCE_PROJECT_TOOLTIP]Science Projects[/TIP] quickly.
Triumph: Round Earther
There are City Projects that will help us understand the nature of our own world and the cosmos beyond.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] are special, optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. The Scientific Triumphs are a good match if you’re pursuing a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP]. [nn]There are two types of Triumphs. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age. You can only select a limited number of Dedications at the start of each Age, though, so keep that in mind as you pursue them. [nn]Triumphs can provide extra challenges and reward playstyles different from the ones you may normally try. When you’re ready to push yourself, give them a shot!
Something to Try…

The [b]Round Earther [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumph[/TIP] requires you to complete the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP] [b]Chart the Stars and Spherical Earth[/b] before the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP] ends. To unlock the Projects, research both [b]Navigation[/b] and [b]Mathematics[/b] in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech Tree[/TIP]. You’ll need a high amount of [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] to do so, and you’ll also need at least one [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] with a high amount of [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] to complete the Projects. [nn]This is a challenging Triumph and may take you a few tries to complete, but doing so will prove that you can compete for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP]!
Economic Victory
Economic Victory is merely a matter of controlling the world’s bounty. Follow me, and it will be yours.

There are four ways to achieve a victory in Civilization: Cultural, Military, Scientific, and Economic. The first leader that achieves any of these victories wins the game. [nn]To win an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP], you must have the highest [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP]. Several things contribute to your GDP each turn depending on Researched Technologies, including assigning [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] and active [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP]. Later, you’ll be able to push that further by capturing exotic treasures and having active factories. [nn]Basically, you need to dominate the world’s economy. [nn]To see your GDP and how you rank against the other leaders, visit the [b]Victory Panel[/b]. As the game progresses, you’ll see the number of points required to win the game. It’s not possible to win a Economic Victory in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], so you’ll learn more about that later.
Keep this in mind...

To set yourself up for success early in the game, acquire as many [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] as possible. A great way to do this is to found new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] near clusters of Resources. Your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Economic Advisor[/TIP] will introduce [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] later, but they’re also an important source!
Growing Population
The larger our empire is, the greater it can be. Look for ways to increase our Food yields.

Growing an Empire requires [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b]. Each turn, the [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] each [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] produces goes toward increasing the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP] of that Settlement. When progress is complete, the Settlement receives a new Population that can improve a tile or eventually become a [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialist[/TIP]. [nn]Whenever a Settlement is ready to Grow, you'll be asked which tile you'd like to add that new Population to. This improves the tile into a [b]Farm[/b], [b]Mine[/b], or other type, and the Settlement receives the new yields of that tile. It also expands the border of that Settlement, claiming those new tiles as part of your Empire. [nn]Finally, if the tile has a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP], you’ll gain access to it when you improve that tile.
Keep this in mind...

Try to maximize the yields that are most helpful to you each time you [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP]. Early in the game, focus on tiles that provide the most [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b]. A large Population will help you by providing stronger yields across your empire and giving you access to more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP].
Warehouse Buildings
Warehouse Buildings make our Improvements more productive, and since they're Ageless they'll keep working in every Age.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouse[/TIP][b] [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], like the [b]Granary[/b] or [b]Fishing Quay[/b], increase the yields of improved tiles. Early in the game, each Warehouse Building provides +1 [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] or [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] to each associated [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvement[/TIP]. That will increase as you research new Technologies. [nn]Warehouse Buildings are [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGELESS_TOOLTIP]Ageless[/TIP], which means they’re fully productive and available to build in every [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] once unlocked. Once constructed, they can’t be moved or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_OVERBUILDABLE_TOOLTIP]Overbuilt[/TIP], so it’s important to plan where to build them carefully. [nn]Considering when to spend [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] or [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] to construct Warehouses is a vital skill when managing your empire!
Something to try...

Determine which [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouse[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] will provide the highest [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] benefit to help you [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP] faster then construct it. This is likely either a Granary or Fishing Quay at this stage in the game. The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]’s [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] list displays the number of Warehouse Bonuses the Building immediately provides.
Resources
Make sure to improve all our available Resources, and import any that we lack. Let's not leave food on the table.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], such as [b]Silk[/b] or [b]Iron[/b], provide special bonuses when you improve the tile they're found on or receive them through [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP]. They can be found throughout the map and are identified by their unique icons. [nn]In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], there are [b]three types[/b] of Resources. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMPIRE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Empire Resources[/TIP], such as Iron, provide passive effects to your entire empire. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BONUS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Bonus Resources[/TIP], like Fish, provide bonus yields when assigned to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]City Resources[/TIP], like Silk, are even more powerful, but they can only be assigned to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP]. [nn]When Bonus and City Resources are assigned after Researching The Wheel, they provide [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP] each turn. [b]Assigned Resources[/b] are a very important source of GDP. Managing your empire's Resources is helpful for all Victory types, but it's crucial when pursuing an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP].
Something to try...

Improve a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BONUS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Bonus Resource[/TIP] the next time a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grows[/TIP], then assign it. If there are no City or Bonus Resources nearby, either expand your borders until you can reach one or found a new Settlement. Note that you can only [b]assign or unassign [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] on the same turn you gained a new Resource or [b]Resource Slot[/b].
Trade Routes
No marketplace survives in isolation. With Merchants, we can create Trade Routes with other Civilizations and gain their Resources.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] are a great way to gain access to additional [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP]. Once established, a Trade Route provides a copy of each Resource improved by a foreign [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] to your empire, and the other Leader receives bonus [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] each turn. Importantly, both of these benefits are provided for free – it does not cost you [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] and the other side does not lose access to their Resources! [nn]Trade Routes are established by Merchant units. In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ANTIQUITY_AGE_TOOLTIP]Antiquity Age[/TIP], the Merchant must travel to the destination Settlement before establishing the Trade Route, but once established, you’ll immediately gain access to the Resources. [nn]In order to establish a Trade Route, you must have [b]Trade Route Capacity[/b] with the leader. By default, you can establish one Trade Route per leader, but you can increase this limit with the Improve Trade Relations diplomatic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ENDEAVOR_TOOLTIP]Endeavor[/TIP]. [nn]In addition, the foreign Settlement must be within range of one of your Settlements. In the Antiquity Age, this range is 10 by land and 30 by sea. Some abilities can increase this range, as can the [b]Trade Outpost [/b][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP][b] Focus[/b]. Keep in mind that the land range is actual traversable range, so Mountains and other terrain features must be navigated around. [nn]Trade Routes last through the end of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], but they end if you go to War with the other leader or if the Trade Route is plundered by a hostile unit.
Something to try...

After training a [b]Merchant[/b], select it to see a list of all available [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP]. Look for locations that provide a large number of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], especially key Resources that are particularly valuable to your strategy. Favor Trade Routes with friendlier leaders since you’re less likely to go to War with them and lose all your Trade Routes. [nn]Finally, consider the safety of the Trade Route! Sending Trade Routes through dangerous territory is risky. Either protect them with [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] or send your Merchants to safer lands.
Connected Towns
Towns share their Food with Cities they're connected to.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] are an excellent source of [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] and [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] for your empire. [nn]Instead of training Units or constructing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], Towns convert all their [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b][b] into [/b][icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b]. This [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] is sent straight to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURY_TOOLTIP]Treasury[/TIP] like any other. [nn]Towns also have the ability to control how their [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] is used. By default, Towns start in a Growing Focus. This allows the Town to use its [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP] its own Population. When the Town is later set to any other [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_FOCUS_TOOLTIP]Town Focus[/TIP], it stops growing and instead sends all of its [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to all [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONNECTED_TOOLTIP]Connected Cities[/TIP] evenly. [nn][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] are automatically Connected by land when they are within 10 tiles of each other. This range increases to 15 in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP] and 20 in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP]. A road will indicate that they are Connected. Settlements are automatically Connected by sea when they are on the same [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONTINENT_TOOLTIP]Continent[/TIP] and both have a Water Building.
Something to try...

Once a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] reaches 7 [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Population[/TIP], select a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_FOCUS_TOOLTIP]Town Focus[/TIP] that best benefits your empire and takes advantage of the Town’s strengths. This will stop the Town from growing and instead said all [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONNECTED_TOOLTIP]Connected Cities[/TIP]. Make sure the Town is actually Connected to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] or the [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] will be wasted! [nn]Managing Connected Towns effectively is an important skill for growing your empire. [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] sent to Cities can allow them to use their territory for more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] rather than [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP] like Farms, and it’s helpful for producing more [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] to further boost your yields.
Resource Slots
We must Slot Bonus and City Resources to gain their benefits. Look for ways to gain additional Resources Slots if space is limited.

The Bonus and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]City Resources[/TIP] we collect can be assigned to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] for additional benefits. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BONUS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Bonus Resources[/TIP], like Fish, provide bonus yields when assigned to a Settlement. City Resources, like Silk, are even more powerful, but they can only be assigned to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP]. [nn]In order to assign a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP], there must be a free Resource Slot in the Settlement. You can add more Resource Slots by constructing [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], like Markets, and certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]. Certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GOVERNMENT_TOOLTIP]Government[/TIP] Policies or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADITION_TOOLTIP]Traditions[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-State[/TIP] Bonuses, and Economic [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP] also provide additional Resource slots. Even the Resource Camels will add bonus slots to whichever City it’s assigned to! [nn]Resources can only be assigned or unassigned on the same turn in which you earn a new Resource or Resource Slot.
Something to try...

When you need another [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] Slot in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP], build a Market or a Lighthouse. If you still need more slots, look for Camels in your empire or start a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Route[/TIP] with a neighbor who has access to Camels.
Economic Victory Scoring
There are many ways to increase our GDP. In order to win, we'll need to diversify.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they achieve economic dominance against all other leaders. This dominance is measured by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP]. The following contribute to your GDP each turn: [nn]- [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP]: Gold Buildings after Researching the Currency Mastery, from the current [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], provide 2 points per turn. [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BONUS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Bonus Resources[/TIP]: City and Bonus Resources, when assigned to a City after Researching The Wheel, provide 1 point of GDP per turn if the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] is local or 1 point of GDP per turn if the Resource is imported via a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Route[/TIP]. Resources provide no GDP when assigned to a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP]. [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoys[/TIP]: Exclusive to the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], each returned Treasure Convoy provides 20 points of GDP per Cargo. This amount scales by Game Speed. [n]- [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FACTORY_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Factory Resources[/TIP]: Exclusive to the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP], Factory Resources provide 2 points of GDP per turn when assigned to a City or Town. [nn]Certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] in the Modern Age also provide GDP. [nn]Starting in the Exploration Age, a winner is declared if the first place leader has 6x the points of the second place leader. As time goes on, that requirement lowers until only 1.25x is required toward the end of the Modern Age. See the Victory screen for more information.
Keep in Mind...

There are many ways to win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP], but the bottom line is you need the most active economy. Look for opportunities to secure [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], start [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP], return [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoys[/TIP], and construct [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP]. As time goes on, the amount you need to dominate other leaders is reduced, making victory more achievable.
Triumph: Abundance
We can never have too many Resources. With an abundance of them, we'll have the world eating out of our hands.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] are special, optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age. You can only select a limited number of Dedications at the start of each Age, though, so keep that in mind as you pursue them. With the dawn of a new Age, victory appears on the horizon at last. Let us strive ever toward it.

[nn]For the first time, victory is now possible. If we cannot create enough Tourism on our own, perhaps we should look to hamper others'.

To win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP], you need to make sure nobody beats you to it. One strategy, of course, is to earn points faster. However, that’s not the only option. [nn]Since the Cultural Victory is scored in part by having [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NATURAL_WONDER_TOOLTIP]Natural Wonders[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Unique Improvements[/TIP] in your empire, another strategy is to ensure your opponents have fewer in theirs. Founding a Religion
With our own Religion, we can spread our beliefs, gather Relics, and attract pilgrims – Tourists, of a sort.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIGION_TOOLTIP]Religion[/TIP] is a core gameplay mechanic in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP]. Religions provide bonuses to your empire as you use Missionaries to spread your Religion, and they’re the primary way to collect [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIC_TOOLTIP]Relics[/TIP]. [nn]To found your own Religion, you need to build a Temple in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]. This Settlement becomes your Holy [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP]. Temples are [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] unlocked by the Piety [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civic[/TIP]. [nn]Once your Temple finishes construction, you’ll be asked to found your Religion by selecting a name, icon, and two beliefs. Reliquary Beliefs determine how your Religion generates Relics. Founder Beliefs determine your bonuses as you convert Settlements to your Religion. These cannot be changed later in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], so think about your future strategy. Some Beliefs cannot be shared between Religions, so founding your Religion early can give you a strategic lead. [nn]Founding a Religion also unlocks the Theology Civics Tree. Using Missionaries
Missionaries are the agents of our Religion and the primary way we earn Relics.

Missionaries are a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVILIAN_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Civilian Unit[/TIP] used to spread your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIGION_TOOLTIP]Religion[/TIP]. In order to train Missionaries, you first need to found a Religion. Once founded, you can train Missionaries in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] with a Temple. [nn]Missionaries can convert a Settlement to your Religion. Settlements have both Urban and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RURAL_TOOLTIP]Rural[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Populations[/TIP], each with their own Religion., A Settlement is only fully following a Religion when both its Urban and Rural Populations follow the same Religion. Spreading your Religion both within your empire and abroad is important to get the most benefit out of your Religion. [nn]To convert an Urban Population, the Missionary must use the Spread Religion action on an Urban [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTRICT_TOOLTIP]District[/TIP]. Similarly, to convert a Rural Population, the Missionary must use the same action on a Rural tile. If the Settlement had no prior Religion, spreading to either type will count for both, giving an advantage to players who are first to send out Missionaries. [nn]Once a Settlement has been converted, it will generate a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIC_TOOLTIP]Relic[/TIP] if it meets the condition of your Reliquary Belief, and it will begin providing any religious benefits to your empire.

As we practice our faith, we create Great Works known as Relics. House them in places with Great Work Slots such as Temples to attract pilgrims.

A [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIC_TOOLTIP]Relic[/TIP] is a cultural [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Work[/TIP] produced through various means. Once produced, Relics can be displayed in any [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] with a Great Work Slot to provide bonus [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b], [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b], and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP]. [nn]The primary way to produce a Relic is by converting [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIGION_TOOLTIP]Religion[/TIP]. They can also be produced when studying certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVIC_TOOLTIP]Civics[/TIP] or researching certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Techs[/TIP], becoming [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SUZERAIN_TOOLTIP]Suzerain[/TIP] of Cultural [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITY_STATE_TOOLTIP]City-States[/TIP], and constructing certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]. [nn]Relics must be displayed to grant bonus [icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] and [icon:YIELD_CULTURE][b]Culture[/b]. In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], your Palace, Temples, and certain Wonders all grant Great Work Slots. Be sure to construct enough Buildings with Slots to take full advantage of your Relics.

Advanced Production
A devout society is a productive society. Allow me to explain.

Optimizing our [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] is more than just improving Mines and Woodcutters. [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] is the raw output of your people, and you’ll need some tricks up your sleeve if you want to compete for [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP]. [nn]First, [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAREHOUSE_TOOLTIP]Warehouses[/TIP], like the Sawmill and Harbor, are very important. Focus on the Warehouses that best match the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP] to maximize the Warehouse bonus. [nn]Next, [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] is important for [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. The more [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] a Settlement receives, the faster it can [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP] and gain access to more yields. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] can provide [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONNECTED_TOOLTIP]Connected Cities[/TIP] by setting a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_FOCUS_TOOLTIP]Town Focus[/TIP]. This is a very effective way to help your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] Grow. [nn]Remember that you can reassign [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP] every time a Resource or Resource Slot is added to your empire. If you’re constructing a Wonder, it’s often a good idea to move all [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] Resources to that City. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMPIRE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Empire Resources[/TIP] that boost Wonder [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] can also help – if none are in your empire, you may be able to start a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Route[/TIP] for some. [nn]Certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SOCIAL_POLICY_TOOLTIP]Social Policies[/TIP] can also have a big impact on [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b]. Some policies provide raw [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] output when conditions are met. Others provide bonus [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] toward certain types of items. Efficiently taking advantage of these bonuses is an important skill. [nn][icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS][b]Happiness[/b] is also key. Unhappy Settlements take a penalty on all yields, and this can be very significant for very unhappy Settlements. [nn]Finally, consider how [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] can be put to use. Purchasing items can keep your [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] queue available for Wonders. Your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Economic Advisor[/TIP] can provide tips on how to maximize [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] yields.
Keep in Mind…

Remember that [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] can snowball. Getting an early boost on [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] lets you construct more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] that can then provide [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b], [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b], and [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b], allowing you to further enhance your [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b].

The oceans, lakes, and rivers of the world are full of more than fish and sand. Now more than ever in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], Naval Units are a necessity in War. Reaching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP] means crossing the Deep Ocean, where Naval and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMBARK_TOOLTIP]Embarked[/TIP] Units have reduced movement and take damage in Rough Seas. [nn]Naval Units are capable of dealing massive damage when under the guidance of a Fleet [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] who functions similarly to an Army Commander. [nn]Not to be confused with Embarked Units, the Naval Unit is only able to traverse water biomes and cannot disembark onto land biomes. Naval Units are what you’ll want in the water surrounding your Armies to take and overwhelm enemy coastal [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP].
Something to try…

In this [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], there are Discoveries in the Deep Ocean that only [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVAL_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Naval Units[/TIP] can reach before you research Shipbuilding. Try claiming one and selecting a reward!
Siege Units
Siege Units such as Catapults and Trebuchets can make short work of enemy Fortifications.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SIEGE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Siege Units[/TIP] are special [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] that are particularly strong against [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORTIFIED_DISTRICTS_TOOLTIP]Fortified Districts[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVAL_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Naval Units[/TIP]. [nn]Employing Siege Units to attack Fortified Districts speeds up their capture thanks to the Units’ high Bombard Strength. When attacking Fortified Districts, Siege Units damage both the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WALL_TOOLTIP]Walls[/TIP] and the Units cowering behind them at once. [nn]Against Naval Units, Siege Units are similarly unmatched. A few Ballistae will send a horde of approaching Cogs to the bottom of the sea. [nn]Siege Units are cumbersome, with lower Movement Speed than other Units of their respective tier, and they’re generally vulnerable to attack. Be sure to keep them well-protected as they move across the battlefield.
Something to Try

Sieging a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]? Don’t forget to bring along a few [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SIEGE_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Siege Units[/TIP] to quickly deal with their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FORTIFIED_DISTRICTS_TOOLTIP]Fortified Districts[/TIP].
Pillaging
Pillaging with a Military Unit can grant important yields and even restore Health.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_IMPROVEMENT_TOOLTIP]Improvements[/TIP] contain valuable prizes of War. The act of Pillaging them returns a combination of Healing and Yields from the targeted constructible. This is an excellent way to keep your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP] healthy while they’re in enemy territory. [nn]While [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_LAND_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Land Units[/TIP] Pillage, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVAL_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Naval Units[/TIP] participate in Coastal Raiding. This allows the Naval Unit to receive Healing and Yields from coastal Buildings and Improvements in a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP]. Discoveries on the coast can also be triggered by Coastal Raiding. [nn]Certain Units and Abilities, as well as certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotions[/TIP], can boost the potency of Pillaging. The defending party must also Repair the Pillaged item to regain its benefits, costing them precious [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] or [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b].
Something to Try
When running low on Health in enemy territory, Pillage a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RURAL_TOOLTIP]Rural[/TIP] tile to receive some healing.
Fortifying
Lacking permanent Fortifications, Military Units can Fortify to gain temporary defensive bonuses.

When a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Unit[/TIP] uses the Fortify action, it begins constructing Temporary Fortifications. Once complete, they provide a bonus to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMBAT_STRENGTH_TOOLTIP]Combat Strength[/TIP] when attacked. Temporary fortifications are useful when enemies approach and you expect an attack or to secure a key piece of terrain in case of a surprise attack. [nn]The Fortify action cannot be used in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]City[/TIP] Centers, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] Centers, or any tile with a permanent Fortification. [nn]Keep in mind if a turn is spent with no Military Unit maintaining them, they collapse and disappear from the map.
Keep in Mind…

Fortifying takes time. Certain [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotions[/TIP] and abilities can speed up how long it takes for a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Unit[/TIP] to create Fortifications.
Peace Deals
Peace Deals put a welcome end to hostilities, and they're a way to gain new Settlements.

There are two ways to end a War: fully eliminate the opponent or strike a Peace Deal. Peace Deals can be proposed after ten turns of War by either party involved. [nn][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] can be offered or requested in the proposal for peace, and the receiving Leader can accept or reject the proposed trade. Leaders are more likely to accept a Peace Deal if they feel what they’re receiving outweighs the cost of continued War. If they’re losing badly and have high [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WAR_WEARINESS_TOOLTIP]War Weariness[/TIP], they may even be willing to give up additional Settlements for peace. [nn]Once Settlements are traded in the Peace Deal, the War is ended and the claimed Settlements change hands. Settlements do not enter [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNREST_TOOLTIP]Unrest[/TIP] when they are peacefully transferred in this way.
Keep in Mind…
While [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] Captured during Wars go into [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNREST_TOOLTIP]Unrest[/TIP], Settlements traded in Peace Deals do not.
Reinforcing
Military Units can Reinforce Armies, automatically sending them to Commanders to provide support.

Army [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commanders[/TIP] provide more than just combat bonuses for your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Units[/TIP]. They also act as a rallying flag for new, incoming Units from across your empire. [nn]It’s often important to send fresh Units to the front line when you’re at War. Instead of individually moving them, you can use the Reinforce Army action on the Military Unit. This causes that Unit to vanish from the map and automatically travel to the selected Army Commander. [nn]After a number of turns based on Movement Speed and the terrain, the Unit will appear stacked in the Army Commander. Any number of Units can Reinforce the Commander at one time, and if the Army Commander is full when they arrive, they’ll appear nearby. [nn]Any Land Military Unit within friendly territory and at full Health can use the Reinforce Army action. Note that there must be a viable path to the Commander, and Commanders that are too close are ineligible.
Something to Try…

Select a Land [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Military Unit[/TIP] at full Health in friendly territory and choose the Reinforce Army action. Find an eligible Army [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_COMMANDER_TOOLTIP]Commander[/TIP] and select it. After some turns, the Unit will appear with the Army Commander. You can monitor progress by selecting the Army Commander.
Distant Lands
There's opportunity in Distant Lands, but the ocean will be dangerous to cross until we Research Shipbuilding.

With the start of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], you can now access [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP]. [nn]Distant Lands territory is any area that requires crossing the Ocean to reach. This can range from small islands dotting the Ocean to entire [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CONTINENT_TOOLTIP]Continents[/TIP] filled with other empires you haven’t yet met. Distant Lands provide new opportunities to expand your empire, secure [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resources[/TIP], and make new allies and enemies. [nn]At first, only your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVAL_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Naval Units[/TIP] can enter the Ocean, and they’re vulnerable to the Rough Seas. This means they can only move one tile at a time in Ocean tiles, and they’ll take damage every time they start their turn there. This makes crossing great distances slow and difficult. [nn]As you research new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP], other Units will be able to enter the Ocean, and you’ll eventually be able to overcome the damage and movement penalties by researching Shipbuilding.
Something to Try…

Send some [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVAL_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Naval Units[/TIP] out into the Ocean to discover [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP]. Be careful as they cross the Ocean, because they’ll take damage each turn. Look for lighter blue Marine tiles where the ships can repair damage before they are destroyed. [nn]If you want to be a true naval power, research Shipbuilding as early as possible to remove the Rough Seas penalty.
Triumph: Master and Commander
The best leaders are born of adversity. Let's see if one of our Fleet Commanders has what it takes.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] are special, optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. The Military Triumphs are a good match if you’re pursuing a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP]. [nn]There are two types of Triumphs. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age.
Keep in Mind…

The Master and Commander [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumph[/TIP] is an excellent Triumph to pursue when you’re pursuing the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MILITARY_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Military Victory[/TIP], since it’s important to have a strong and active Fleet Commander. [nn]Your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_NAVAL_UNITS_TOOLTIP]Naval Units[/TIP] are an important part of conquest in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], and they should be supported by a Fleet Commander. Train one early, and be sure to have them accompany your Naval Units like an Army Commander would. To earn 8 [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROMOTION_TOOLTIP]Promotions[/TIP], you’ll likely need to have a prolonged War with many Naval skirmishes and coastal [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] captured. This is a challenging Triumph and may take you a few tries.
Scientific Victory in Exploration
We cannot win the Space Race until the next Age, but there is much we can, and should, do now.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP] has begun! This new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] provides new gameplay mechanics, like [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_OVERBUILDABLE_TOOLTIP]Overbuilding[/TIP], and the first opportunity to cross the sea and reach [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP]. [nn]For the first time, victory is now possible in the Cultural, Economic, and Military paths. The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPACE_RACE_TOOLTIP]Space Race[/TIP] continues, of course, but cannot be achieved until a Launch Pad is constructed in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP]. [nn]For now, continue to earn as many Innovation as you can through researching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MASTERY_TOOLTIP]Tech Masteries[/TIP], completing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP], and other methods. Keep an eye on the other victory conditions, and if any opponents get close, be sure to disrupt their plans. [nn]Once you reach the end of the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech Tree[/TIP], you can research Future Tech to speed up Age progression. This will make it harder for your opponents to win before the end of the Exploration Age.
Keep this in mind…

With new mechanics come new opportunities. Use [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_OVERBUILDABLE_TOOLTIP]Overbuilding[/TIP] to replace the previous [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] with more advanced ones, increasing the output of your [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP].
Scientific Victory Counterplay
Let us be sure that our opponents aren't leading the Space Race. If they are, we must slow them down.

To win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP], you need to make sure nobody beats you to it. While it’s not yet possible to win a Scientific Victory, we can set ourselves up to be the frontrunner now. [nn]The best option, of course, is to ensure we’re earning as many Innovation as possible, as quickly as possible. There are some things we can do, though, to slow down the progress of others. [nn]First, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SANCTION_TOOLTIP]Sanctions[/TIP] can be a powerful tool. Hinder Research will reduce a leader’s [icon:YIELD_SCIENCE][b]Science[/b] yield by 10%, directly slowing down their ability to research new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP]. Worker Disruption slows their [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP], making it harder for them to complete [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENCE_PROJECT_TOOLTIP]Scientific Projects[/TIP] or secure a key Wonder. The other leader won’t like it, so be prepared to make a quick enemy. [nn]Of course, War is always an option. Capturing some [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] from an opponent is a blunt way to reduce their yields and boost your own.
Keep in Mind…
Remember, if you have trouble getting ahead of an opponent on your own, you can always knock them down.
Overbuilding
The Buildings of the previous Age have become obsolete, but we can Overbuild them with new ones.

When a new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] begins, several changes occur in your empire. An important yet often overlooked change is that most of your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] built in the previous Age lose their Adjacency Bonuses and other effects. This impacts the yield the Building provides directly as well as any bonuses received from [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP]. [nn]This means that you’re now paying for the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAINTENANCE_TOOLTIP]Maintenance[/TIP] of the Building plus any Specialists on the tile with little benefit. The solution is to [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_OVERBUILDABLE_TOOLTIP]Overbuild[/TIP]. [nn]Overbuilding allows you to construct a new Building on top one from a previous Age, replacing the outdated Building. Overbuilding also takes advantage of the existing Building’s materials, using less [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION][b]Production[/b] to construct the new Building. Once constructed, the new Building has full access to its Adjacency Bonuses and other effects. [nn]It’s important to advance your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP] to unlock new Buildings from this Age so you can replace your previous ones. This way, you’ll stay competitive and make the most of the precious space in your empire.
Something to Try…

Once unlocked, construct an Observatory over a Library, Academy, or other [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Building[/TIP] from the previous [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. When placing the Observatory, look for locations that provide high Adjacency Bonuses and have a Building marked as [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_OVERBUILDABLE_TOOLTIP]Overbuildable[/TIP].
Triumph: Enlightenment
Let us see how much total yield our Districts can produce. A challenge, to be sure, but a rewarding one.

[TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumphs[/TIP] are special, optional challenges you can complete in an [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP]. Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. The Scientific Triumphs are a good match if you’re pursuing a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP]. [nn]There are two types of Triumphs. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age. [nn]You can only select three Dedications at the start of each Age, though, so keep that in mind as you pursue them. [nn]Triumphs can provide extra challenges and reward playstyles different from the ones you may normally try. When you’re ready to push yourself, give them a shot.
Keep in Mind…

The Enlightenment [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumph[/TIP] is an excellent Triumph to pursue when you’re pursuing the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SCIENTIFIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Scientific Victory[/TIP], since it requires setting up some very powerful yields across your empire. This is important for both researching [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TECH_TOOLTIP]Tech[/TIP] quickly and completing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_PROJECTS_TOOLTIP]Projects[/TIP]. [nn]To gain such yields in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP], you’ll need to take advantage of strong Adjacency Bonuses, construct high tier [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP], and place [icon:SPECIALIST][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SPECIALIST_TOOLTIP]Specialists[/TIP] where they provide the highest bonuses. Remember to use your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] to feed your Cities so that they have plenty of [icon:YIELD_FOOD][b]Food[/b] to produce new Specialists. This is a challenging Triumph and may take you a few tries.
Economic Victory in Exploration
If we want to win, now is our chance. But don't expect it to be easy. Let me show you what we're up against.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP] has begun! This new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP] provides new gameplay mechanics, like [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resources[/TIP], and the first opportunity to cross the sea and reach [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP]. [nn]For the first time, victory is now possible. The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they achieve economic dominance against all other leaders. This is measured by [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP], which you’ve been earning with every [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] assigned to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CITIES_TOOLTIP]Cities[/TIP] and [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_BUILDINGS_TOOLTIP]Buildings[/TIP] constructed throughout your empire. [nn]At first, the amount of economic dominance you need to achieve is extremely high. Victory this early is only awarded to those who have 6x the score of the next best player. This Transcendent Victory is very difficult to achieve. [nn]As the Exploration Age continues, this threshold is reduced. At 50% [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_PROGRESS_TOOLTIP]Age Progress[/TIP] you’ll earn a Crushing Victory if you achieve 4x the score of the next best player. Later at 75% Age Progress, the threshold is reduced again to 4x and awards the Decisive Victory. [nn]If no victor is declared, which is common, the game continues into the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP].
Keep this in mind…

With new mechanics come new opportunities. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoys[/TIP] returned from [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP] can provide large boosts of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP].
Economic Victory Conditions Lowered
Trade dominance has just become easier. Let's look at the numbers.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they achieve economic dominance against all other leaders. This is represented as a score you must reach above the second place player. [nn]At first, the amount of economic dominance you need to achieve is extremely high. Achieving Victory very early awards the Transcendent Victory, and it’s very difficult to achieve. As the game continues, the threshold lowers as follows: [nn]- Transcendent Victory ([TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP] 0% - 49%): 6x points [n]- Crushing Victory (Exploration Age 50% - 74%): 4x points [n]- Decisive Victory (Exploration Age 75% - [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP] 49%): 3x points [n]- Momentous Victory (Modern Age 50% - 74%): 2x points [n]- Substantive Victory (Modern Age 75% - 89%): 1.5x points [n]- Narrow Victory (Modern Age 90% - 100%): 1.25x points
Keep in Mind…
Victory thresholds have changed. Check the Victory screen to see how you stand against the other leaders.
Economic Victory Counterplay
We must reap the world’s bounty before others can. If we can't raise our GDP, let's at least make things harder for our opponents.

To win the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP], you need to make sure nobody beats you to it. One strategy, of course, is to earn points faster. However, that’s not the only option. [nn]Since the Economic Victory is scored in part by using [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resources[/TIP], another strategy is to ensure your opponents have less access to them. When you’re expanding your territory, prioritize securing land with Resources before your opponents can. This applies both to settling new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Towns[/TIP] and when expanding your borders. [nn][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP] are another major source of Resources, and imported Resources are worth more [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP]. The only way to prevent your opponent from sending you Trade Routes is to declare War. That may be an extreme option, but if you and a few allies join a Joint War against them, they’ll lose access to a major part of the world market. [nn]In the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP], [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoys[/TIP] can provide a steady stream of GDP. Capturing [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP] territory rich with [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resources[/TIP] can prevent your opponents from acquiring them, and failing that remember that you can capture an opponent’s Treasure Convoy by attacking it. [nn][TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SANCTION_TOOLTIP]Sanctions[/TIP] can also slow down a leader’s ability to generate GDP. Hinder Finances will reduce their [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] output by 10%, and Hinder Agriculture can slow their growth so they can’t capture Resources as quickly. They won’t like it if you Sanction them, though, so be prepared to make a quick enemy.
Something to Try…

If you’re unable to catch up with an opponent’s [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP], War is always an option. Consult with your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ADVISOR_TOOLTIP]Military Advisor[/TIP] on tips for waging War.
Economic Victory Countdown
We’ve proven ourselves worthy of the world’s bounty. We're just a countdown away from victory.

To secure the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP], you first need to reach the target [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP] score. When that happens, a five turn countdown begins. This gives you an opportunity to prove your dominance and your opponents an opportunity to challenge your victory. [nn]If at any point your score falls below the target, the countdown pauses. You can fall below the target score if the second place player earns enough points to push the target higher. Your progress on the countdown remains, though, so if you regain dominance you continue from where you left off. [nn]Once the countdown completes, victory is secured and the game is complete! That is, unless you decide to go just One More Turn…
Keep in Mind…
Don’t let your guard down. Anything can happen in these final turns.
Treasure Resources
The world now has Treasure Resources. If we improve those that are in Distant Lands, we'll gain GDP.

A new type of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] is now available in the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP]: [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resources[/TIP]. [nn]Treasure Resources are a special type of [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EMPIRE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Empire Resource[/TIP]. Like Empire Resources, they provide passive buffs to your empire as you collect them by improving their tile or receiving them via [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRADE_ROUTE_TOOLTIP]Trade Routes[/TIP]. [nn]In addition, when a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP] has at least one improved Treasure Resource, it will periodically generate a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoy[/TIP]. This special Unit can be brought back to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_HOMELANDS_TOOLTIP]Homelands[/TIP] to earn a large [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP] boost. [nn]You can see the Treasure Resources you have access to along with the status of any Settlements generating Treasure Convoys in the Commerce screen.
Keep in Mind…

While some Civilizations, Leaders, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], or other effects may allow you to do so, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resources[/TIP] in your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_HOMELANDS_TOOLTIP]Homelands[/TIP] typically do not generate [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoys[/TIP]. If you’re ever unsure if a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Resource[/TIP] is in the Homelands or [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP], hover over the tile.
Treasure Convoys
After we improve Treasure Resources in Distant Lands, we'll begin generating Treasure Convoys. Make sure they get to our Homelands safely.

A [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoy[/TIP] is a special [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_EXPLORATION_AGE_TOOLTIP]Exploration Age[/TIP] [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CIVILIAN_UNIT_TOOLTIP]Civilian Unit[/TIP]. When a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP] has at least one improved [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resource[/TIP], it will periodically generate a Treasure Convoy. [nn]Once generated, the Treasure Convoy can be brought back to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_HOMELANDS_TOOLTIP]Homelands[/TIP] to unload its cargo. Doing so will provide a large boost to [icon:YIELD_GOLD][b]Gold[/b] and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP] for each improved Treasure Resource at the Settlement that generated it. Treasure Convoys are capable of traveling over both land and sea. [nn]Treasure Convoys can be captured by hostile units. When a Unit reduces the Treasure Convoy’s Health to 0, it becomes property of the attacking leader. You may need to protect your Treasure Convoys if they need to travel through enemy territory. You should also make sure Rough Seas do not destroy a Treasure Convoy on its way home. [nn]Some Leaders, Civilizations, [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], and other effects may allow you to generate Treasure Convoys via other means. You can see the status of any Settlements generating Treasure Convoys in the Commerce screen.
Something to Try…

Settle a new [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOWN_TOOLTIP]Town[/TIP] in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP] within range of a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resource[/TIP]. Improve the Treasure Resource during a Growth Event, then check the status in the Treasure tab of the Commerce Screen. Once the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoy[/TIP] spawns, bring it back to your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_HOMELANDS_TOOLTIP]Homelands[/TIP] and use the Unload Cargo action.
Triumph: Treasure Fleet
If we amass enough GDP from Treasure Convoys, this Triumph will be ours.

Each Triumph is themed after one of the game’s six [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ATTRIBUTE_TOOLTIP]Attributes[/TIP]: Cultural, Scientific, Military, Diplomatic, Expansionist, and Economic. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MINOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Minor Triumphs[/TIP] are a bit easier to accomplish, and they provide an instant boost when completed. [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MAJOR_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Major Triumphs[/TIP] are truly challenging commitments, and completing them unlocks a powerful [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DEDICATION_TOOLTIP]Dedication[/TIP] you can use at the start of the next Age. The Treasure Fleet [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TRIUMPH_TOOLTIP]Triumph[/TIP] is an excellent Triumph to pursue when you’re pursuing the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ECONOMIC_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Economic Victory[/TIP], since accumulating the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_CONVOY_TOOLTIP]Treasure Convoys[/TIP] is already something you should be doing to increase [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GDP_TOOLTIP]GDP[/TIP]. [nn]To set yourself up for success, you’ll need to have several [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlements[/TIP] in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_DISTANT_LANDS_TOOLTIP]Distant Lands[/TIP]. Look for locations with access to at least 3 [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TREASURE_RESOURCES_TOOLTIP]Treasure Resources[/TIP] that aren’t too far from your [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_HOMELANDS_TOOLTIP]Homelands[/TIP], and prioritize improving the Treasure Resources when the Settlements [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_POPULATION_TOOLTIP]Grow[/TIP].
Cultural Victory in Modern
The world has changed once again, and with that change come new ways of increasing Tourism.

The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_MODERN_AGE_TOOLTIP]Modern Age[/TIP] has begun! Once again, the ways of the old world give rise to a new one. Where once people built Temples and spread their [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIGION_TOOLTIP]Religions[/TIP], now they seek to celebrate history with Museums and [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ARTIFACT_TOOLTIP]Artifacts[/TIP] from the past. [nn]This is the final [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_AGE_TOOLTIP]Age[/TIP], and as such those who wish to achieve Victory must do so now. The [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CULTURAL_VICTORY_TOOLTIP]Cultural Victory[/TIP] is awarded to a leader when they achieve cultural dominance against all other leaders. This is measured in [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP], which you’ve been accumulating through the prior Ages as you constructed [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_WONDERS_TOOLTIP]Wonders[/TIP], entered [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_CELEBRATIONS_TOOLTIP]Celebrations[/TIP], constructed [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_UNIQUE_BUILDING_TOOLTIP]Unique Buildings[/TIP], collected [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_RELIC_TOOLTIP]Relics[/TIP], and more. [nn]Victory is well within grasp now for any leader on any path. It’s important to balance both your own pursuit of Victory as well as preventing the Victory of others. Pay attention to the scores across each Victory type and react accordingly. As the Modern Age continues, the threshold for Victory will get lower and lower until a Victor is declared.
Keep this in mind…

With new mechanics come new ways to earn [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_TOURISTS_TOOLTIP]Tourism[/TIP]! Train an Explorer and use them to dig up [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_ARTIFACT_TOOLTIP]Artifacts[/TIP] scattered around the world. Displaying these [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_GREAT_WORKS_TOOLTIP]Great Works[/TIP] in Museum provides a large boost to Tourism.

Victory is now easier than ever. Allow me to explain.
